title: Secrets in the pipeline and least privilege

videos.script: A pipeline holds keys. The token for the carrier, the credentials that deploy, the permission to publish a release. {{keys}} This lesson follows one of them, shipquote's carrier token, along every path by which a secret leaves the place it belongs. {{paths}} A commit that is deleted twenty minutes later and still holds the token. A configuration file every user on the machine can read. A token on a command line, printed by ps for anybody who asks. {{leaks}} Then the log. Masking hides the exact value and misses the same value in base64. The only defence that holds is a program that never prints its secrets. {{logs}} Then the pipeline's own permissions, kept to what each job needs. And credentials that expire within the hour, so nothing durable is there to steal. {{privilege}} The lesson ends with rotation. You will watch a careless one cause a small outage, and learn the order that matters after a real leak. Revoke first, clean up last. {{rotation}}
